organizations.name: Monarchy of Bahrain (King of Bahrain)
organizations.description: Constitutional monarchy and head of state of the Kingdom of Bahrain under the 2002 Constitution. The House of Khalifa has ruled since 1783; the ruler held the title of hakim until 1971 and emir until 2002, when Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa proclaimed himself king.

organizations.name: Cabinet of Bahrain
organizations.description: Chief executive body of the Kingdom of Bahrain (Council of Ministers). Under Article 32(b) of the 2002 Constitution executive authority is vested in the King together with the Council of Ministers; the Cabinet is appointed directly by the King.

organizations.name: Council of Representatives of Bahrain
organizations.description: Lower house of the bicameral National Assembly of Bahrain, with 40 members elected by universal suffrage for four-year terms.

organizations.name: Consultative Council (Bahrain)
organizations.description: Upper house (Shura Council) of the National Assembly of Bahrain; its 40 members are appointed directly by the King.

organizations.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
organizations.description: Government ministry responsible for Bahrain's foreign relations, established in 1971 by Amiri Decree upon independence.

organizations.name: Ministry of Interior
organizations.description: Government ministry responsible for law enforcement and public safety in Bahrain; headquartered at the Diwan Fort in Manama.

organizations.name: Ministry of Finance and National Economy
organizations.description: Government ministry responsible for state finances and the national economy, dating to 1970; organizes the budget, customs and treasury functions.

key_people.title: Minister of Finance and National Economy
key_people.name: Shaikh Salman bin Khalifa Al Khalifa

organizations.name: Ministry of Education
organizations.description: Government ministry responsible for public education and higher education licensing in Bahrain.

organizations.name: Ministry of Health
organizations.description: Government ministry operating Bahrain's public health system, including Salmaniya Medical Complex.

organizations.name: Ministry of Justice, Islamic Affairs and Endowment
aliases: Ministry of Justice and Islamic Affairs
organizations.description: Government ministry responsible for the courts administration, Islamic affairs and religious endowments (waqf).

organizations.name: Ministry of Works
organizations.description: Government ministry responsible for public works and infrastructure, established in 1975.

organizations.name: Ministry of Industry and Commerce
organizations.description: Government ministry responsible for industry, commerce and company registration in Bahrain.

organizations.name: Ministry of Labour
aliases: Ministry of Labour and Social Development
organizations.description: Government ministry responsible for labour affairs; the minister concurrently holds the Legal Affairs portfolio.

key_people.title: Minister of Labour and Minister of Legal Affairs
key_people.name: Yousif bin Abdulhussain Khalaf

organizations.name: Information & eGovernment Authority
organizations.description: Bahrain's principal government institution for statistics, census data and national eGovernment services, established in 2015 (succeeding the Central Informatics Organisation).

organizations.name: Electricity and Water Authority
organizations.description: Government authority responsible for electricity and water services in Bahrain.

organizations.name: Labour Market Regulatory Authority
organizations.description: Government body regulating Bahrain's labour market, work permits and sponsorship of migrant workers, established 2006.

organizations.name: Tamkeen (Labour Fund)
organizations.description: Semi-government organisation established 2006 to support private-sector enterprise development and training in Bahrain.

organizations.name: Bahrain Economic Development Board
organizations.description: Public agency responsible for attracting investment and driving economic development; steward of Bahrain Vision 2030.

organizations.name: Supreme Council for Women
organizations.description: Bahrain's advisory body to the government on women's issues, chaired by Sheikha Sabika bint Ibrahim Al Khalifa, wife of the King.

organizations.name: Supreme Judicial Council
organizations.description: Supreme administrative body of Bahrain's judiciary; per Freedom House the King heads the council and appoints judges.

organizations.name: Court of Cassation
organizations.description: Highest court in Bahrain's judicial ladder, created in 1989 to monitor the application of the law.

organizations.name: Constitutional Court of Bahrain
organizations.description: Constitutional court of the Kingdom of Bahrain, established 14 September 2002 under the 2002 Constitution.

organizations.name: Judiciary of Bahrain
organizations.description: Bahrain's court system, divided into Civil Courts, Sharia Courts and Criminal Courts; judges are appointed by the King.

organizations.name: Civil Aviation Affairs
organizations.description: Bahrain's civil aviation regulator, responsible for air transport oversight and Bahrain International Airport affairs.

organizations.name: Bahrain Tourism and Exhibitions Authority
organizations.description: Authority responsible for developing and promoting Bahrain as a tourism destination, established 2015.

organizations.name: Information Affairs Authority
organizations.description: Government agency in charge of information and media affairs (est. 2010); controls the Bahrain News Agency.

organizations.name: National Institution for Human Rights
organizations.description: Bahrain's national human rights institution (NHRI) established in line with the Paris Principles.

organizations.name: Quality Assurance Authority for Education and Training
organizations.description: Independent authority reviewing the quality of education and training provision in Bahrain, established 2008.

organizations.name: Civil Service Bureau
organizations.description: Independent governmental body managing civil service affairs in Bahrain, established 1975.

organizations.name: Social Insurance Organization
organizations.description: State body administering social insurance and pensions in Bahrain.

organizations.name: Bahrain Authority for Culture and Antiquities
organizations.description: Government body responsible for culture, heritage and antiquities in Bahrain.

organizations.name: Isa Cultural Centre
organizations.description: National cultural centre of Bahrain, including the Historical Documents Centre (national archives), inaugurated 18 December 2008.

organizations.name: Mumtalakat Holding Company
organizations.description: Sovereign wealth fund of the Kingdom of Bahrain, holding the state's stakes in key national enterprises including Gulf Air, Alba, Batelco and Bapco Energies.

organizations.name: Bapco Energies
organizations.description: Bahrain's integrated petroleum holding, formerly nogaholding; an agency within the Ministry of Oil and Environment established in 2007 under NOGA and independent since NOGA's abolition in September 2021.

organizations.name: Bahrain Petroleum Company (Bapco)
organizations.description: Bahrain's oil refining company, established 1929, headquartered at Awali; a subsidiary within the Bapco Energies group.

organizations.name: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba)
organizations.description: One of the world's largest aluminium smelters, established 1968 and headquartered at Askar; majority state-owned and listed among Bahrain's major SOEs by the US State Department.

organizations.name: Gulf Air
organizations.description: Flag carrier of Bahrain, founded 1950, headquartered in Muharraq; operates to about 65 destinations in 38 countries from its hub at Bahrain International Airport.

organizations.name: Bahrain Airport Company
organizations.description: Operator and managing body of Bahrain International Airport, fully owned by Mumtalakat and placed under the Gulf Air Group Holding Company.

organizations.name: Gulf Petrochemical Industries Company (GPIC)
organizations.description: Petrochemicals company manufacturing ammonia, methanol and urea at Sitra; an equal joint venture of Bapco Energies (Bahrain), SABIC (Saudi Arabia) and Petrochemical Industries Company (Kuwait), established December 1979.

organizations.name: Banagas (Bahrain Natural Gas Company)
organizations.description: Bahraini natural gas processing and distribution company, established 1979, headquartered at Sakhir.

organizations.name: Batelco (Bahrain Telecommunications Company)
organizations.description: Bahrain's national telecommunications operator, established 1981 and headquartered at Hamala; majority state-owned via Mumtalakat and the Social Insurance Organisation (OECD), now operating under the Beyon group.

organizations.name: Arab Shipbuilding and Repair Yard Company (ASRY)
organizations.description: Shipbuilding and repair yard based at Al Hidd, Bahrain.

organizations.name: Beyon
organizations.description: Bahraini digital and telecoms group (encompassing Batelco), named by the US State Department among Bahrain's major state-owned enterprises in its 2025 Investment Climate Statement.

organizations.name: Investcorp
organizations.description: Global alternative investment firm headquartered in Manama, founded 1982; invests across private equity, real assets, credit and infrastructure. Reported $62.3B assets under management as of July 2026.

organizations.name: Arcapita
organizations.description: Asset management and investment firm founded 1997 and headquartered in Manama, with offices in the US, UK, Saudi Arabia and Singapore; has completed over 100 investments.

organizations.name: Nass Corporation B.S.C.
organizations.description: Bahraini public joint-stock company in industrial and construction services, listed on the Bahrain Bourse since 2005 with paid-up capital of BHD 22 million.

organizations.name: Fakhro Group (Abdulla Yousif Fakhro Group)
organizations.description: Bahraini family-owned conglomerate dating to 1888, active in automotive distribution, ICT, insurance, logistics, real estate and F&B franchising; headquartered in Manama.

organizations.name: Yusuf Bin Ahmed Kanoo (YBA Kanoo)
organizations.description: One of the oldest Gulf family trading conglomerates, active in shipping, travel, energy services and industrial services; ranked among the Top 100 Arab Family Businesses.

organizations.name: Y.K. Almoayyed & Sons
organizations.description: Bahraini family business group spanning electronics, automotive and heavy equipment distribution; listed among the Top 100 Arab Family Businesses (2020).

organizations.name: A.J.M. Kooheji Group
organizations.description: Bahraini family trading and investment group; listed among the Top 100 Arab Family Businesses (2020).

organizations.name: Haji Hassan Group
organizations.description: Bahraini family group focused on building materials and related industries; listed among the Top 100 Arab Family Businesses (2020).

organizations.name: stc Bahrain
organizations.description: Bahraini telecommunications company operating since 2010 under the brand of Saudi Arabia's stc group; about 5,000 employees per Wikidata.

organizations.name: Bahrain Centre for Human Rights
organizations.description: Bahraini non-profit NGO founded by activists in 2002 to promote human rights; issued a dissolution order after its former president Abdulhadi Al Khawaja was arrested in September 2004 for criticising the Prime Minister.

organizations.name: Bahrain Human Rights Society
organizations.description: Human rights organisation set up in 2002 in the wake of wide-ranging political reforms; Wikipedia describes it in the past tense, indicating it is no longer active.

organizations.name: Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy (BIRD)
organizations.description: Non-profit human rights organisation founded in 2013 (headquartered in London) that promotes democratisation and human rights in Bahrain; founded by Sayed Ahmed Alwadaei, Alaa Shehabi and Hussain Abdullah.

organizations.name: Bahrain Human Rights Watch Society
organizations.description: Bahraini human rights organisation established in November 2004, active on women's rights issues.

organizations.name: Bahrain Youth Society for Human Rights
organizations.description: Human rights organisation founded in March 2005, active in the Bahraini uprising; organises training workshops and documents violations; Mohammed Al-Maskati has served as its president.

organizations.name: Bahrain Transparency Society
organizations.description: National chapter of Transparency International in Bahrain (per Wikidata).

organizations.name: Bahrain Women's Union
organizations.description: Umbrella organisation championing women's causes in Bahrain (per Citizens for Bahrain's civil society guide).

organizations.name: University of Bahrain
organizations.description: Bahrain's public university, established by royal decree in 1986; the country's largest higher-education institution with three campuses, more than 30,000 students and nine colleges.

organizations.name: Arabian Gulf University
organizations.description: Regional public university in the Salmaniya area of Manama, established 1980 and governed by the GCC states; entry restricted to GCC nationals.

organizations.name: Ahlia University
organizations.description: Private not-for-profit university in Manama, established 2001 and owned by the Arab Academy for Research and Studies holding company.

organizations.name: Bahrain Polytechnic
organizations.description: Government-owned tertiary education institute established by Royal Decree in July 2008 as a key Bahrain Vision 2030 initiative.

organizations.name: RCSI Bahrain (Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland - Medical University of Bahrain)
organizations.description: Constituent university of the Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland located in Bahrain, established 2004.

organizations.name: American University of Bahrain
organizations.description: Private university in Riffa opened in September 2019; the first purpose-built American-model university in Bahrain, licensed by the Higher Education Council.

organizations.name: AMA International University
organizations.description: Private international university in Bahrain, established 2002.

organizations.name: Applied Science University
organizations.description: Private university in Bahrain, established 2004.

organizations.name: Gulf University
organizations.description: Private university in Sanad, Bahrain, established 2001.

organizations.name: Kingdom University
organizations.description: Private university in Bahrain, established 2001.

organizations.name: Royal University for Women
organizations.description: Private women's university in Bahrain, established 2005.

organizations.name: University College of Bahrain
organizations.description: Private university college in Bahrain, established 2002.

organizations.name: Bahrain Institute of Banking and Finance (BIBF)
organizations.description: Bahrain's training institute for banking, finance and business skills.

organizations.name: Bahrain Centre for Studies and Research
organizations.description: Bahraini research centre established 1981 (per Wikidata).

organizations.name: Bahrain Center for Strategic, International and Energy Studies (Derasat)
organizations.description: Think tank based in Manama focused on strategic, international and energy studies, established 2009.

organizations.name: Bahrain News Agency (BNA)
organizations.description: The state news agency of Bahrain, established 1976; the official conveyor of the Kingdom's news locally and abroad.

organizations.name: Bahrain Radio and Television Corporation
organizations.description: Government-owned public broadcaster headquartered in Manama, under the control of the Information Affairs Authority; state media without independent governing boards (State Media Monitor).

organizations.name: Al Ayam
organizations.description: Arabic newspaper published in Bahrain and based in Manama; Al Ayam Publishing was established 7 March 1989 by a group of young Bahraini journalists including former information minister Nabeel Al Hamer.

organizations.name: Akhbar Al Khaleej
organizations.description: Bahraini Arabic daily publication, sister paper of the English-language Gulf Daily News.

organizations.name: Gulf Daily News
organizations.description: English-language local newspaper published in Bahrain by Dar Akhbar Al Khaleej; one of Bahrain's six dailies, calling itself 'The Voice of Bahrain'.

organizations.name: Daily Tribune
organizations.description: Daily newspaper in Bahrain (per Wikidata, established 1997).

organizations.name: Al-Wasat
organizations.description: Arabic-language national newspaper of Bahrain founded 7 September 2002 (per Wikidata); listed among Bahrain's major national news outlets.

organizations.name: Al-Watan (Bahrain)
organizations.description: Arabic national newspaper covering national news, politics, economy and society (alwatannews.net); listed among Bahrain's major national news outlets.

organizations.name: Trade Arabia
organizations.description: Bahrain-based online business news website for the Gulf region, established 1999.

organizations.name: Central Bank of Bahrain
organizations.description: Bahrain's central bank and financial regulator, a public corporate entity established by the Central Bank of Bahrain and Financial Institutions Law on 6 September 2006.

organizations.name: National Bank of Bahrain
organizations.description: Bahraini public shareholding bank providing retail and wholesale commercial banking, treasury and investment advisory services; licensed by the CBB and listed on the Bahrain Bourse, with overseas branches.

organizations.name: Bank of Bahrain and Kuwait (BBK)
organizations.description: Retail bank established 16 March 1971 in both Bahrain and Kuwait; shareholders include the public and the Government of Bahrain; operates branches in Bahrain, Kuwait and India.

organizations.name: Kuwait Finance House Bahrain (formerly Ahli United Bank)
organizations.description: Regional retail bank, described by Wikipedia as Bahrain's largest bank as Ahli United Bank (AUB); now operating as Kuwait Finance House B.S.C. following acquisition by the KFH group.

organizations.name: Bahrain Islamic Bank (BisB)
organizations.description: Bahrain's first Islamic bank, founded 7 March 1979 and listed on the Bahrain Bourse; supervised by the Central Bank of Bahrain.

organizations.name: Al Salam Bank
organizations.description: Bahraini bank licensed by the Central Bank of Bahrain.

organizations.name: Khaleeji Commercial Bank (KHCB)
organizations.description: Bahraini public shareholding Islamic retail and corporate bank established 2004, headquartered in Manama and licensed by the CBB.

organizations.name: Bank ABC (Arab Banking Corporation)
organizations.description: Conventional wholesale bank licensed by the Central Bank of Bahrain, established 1980; about 3,100 employees.

organizations.name: Gulf International Bank (GIB)
organizations.description: Wholesale bank established 1976, licensed by the Central Bank of Bahrain and headquartered in Manama.

organizations.name: Al Baraka Banking Group
organizations.description: Bahrain-based international Islamic financial group providing retail, corporate, treasury and investment banking through subsidiaries in 13 countries; licensed by the CBB as an Investment Business Firm - Category 1.

organizations.name: GFH Financial Group
organizations.description: Islamic investment bank headquartered at Bahrain Financial Harbour, formerly known as Gulf Finance House.

organizations.name: Bahrain Development Bank
organizations.description: Development finance institution established by the Government of Bahrain to promote investment; registered with the Ministry of Industry and Commerce and licensed by the CBB as a conventional retail bank.

organizations.name: Arab Insurance Group (Arig)
organizations.description: Bahrain-based regional reinsurance company, established 1980.

organizations.name: Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC)
aliases: Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf
organizations.description: Regional intergovernmental political and economic union and military alliance of Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE; charter signed 25 May 1981; headquartered in Riyadh. Bahrain is a founding member.

organizations.name: League of Arab States (Arab League)
organizations.description: Regional organisation of 22 Arab member states headquartered in Cairo; Bahrain is a member state.

organizations.name: Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
organizations.description: Intergovernmental organisation founded 1969 with 57 member states, headquartered in Jeddah; Bahrain is a member state.

organizations.name: United Nations
organizations.description: Global intergovernmental organization; Bahrain is a member state (admitted after independence in 1971).

organizations.name: Accounting and Auditing Organization for Islamic Financial Institutions (AAOIFI)
organizations.description: Bahrain-based not-for-profit organization established 29 March 1991 to develop and promulgate Shariah accounting, auditing and governance standards for the global Islamic finance industry.

organizations.name: MENAFATF
aliases: Middle East and North Africa Financial Action Task Force
organizations.description: Middle East and North Africa Financial Action Task Force, the FATF-style regional body for anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing, with its secretariat in Manama, Bahrain.

organizations.name: Al-Wefaq National Islamic Society
organizations.description: Shia political society that was by far the largest single party in the Bahraini legislature (18 of 40 seats, 2006-2011); ordered closed by Bahrain's highest court (dissolution upheld 2016) and since operating clandestinely.

organizations.name: Al-Asalah Islamic Society
organizations.description: Salafist political society, the main Sunni Salafi grouping in Bahrain, founded 5 June 2002.

organizations.name: Al-Menbar Islamic Society
organizations.description: Political wing of the Sunni Islamist Al-Eslah Society and Bahrain's branch of the Muslim Brotherhood; patron is Shaikh Isa bin Mohammed Al Khalifa, a former labour minister.

organizations.name: National Democratic Action Society (Wa'ad)
organizations.description: Bahrain's largest leftist political society and the first licensed political group in any Gulf state, established 2002; General Secretary Fouad Seyadi (elected November 2016); banned June 2017 on terrorism charges, a move criticised by Amnesty International.

organizations.name: Progressive Democratic Tribune
organizations.description: Political organisation launched in 2001 by returning exiles of the underground communist National Liberation Front - Bahrain; effectively the NLF's successor.

organizations.name: Islamic Action Society
organizations.description: Islamist political society (Amal) mainly appealing to Shia followers of Mohammad Hussaini Shirazi ('the Shirazi faction'); Wikipedia describes it in the past tense as one of Bahrain's main Islamist parties.

organizations.name: Haq Movement
aliases: Haq Movement for Liberty and Democracy
organizations.description: Opposition political organisation founded in November 2005 with Hasan Mushaima as secretary general; several leaders previously in Al-Wefaq's leadership.

organizations.name: Al-Meethaq
organizations.description: Political grouping in Bahrain founded 2002; liberal ideology per Wikidata.

organizations.name: Nationalist Democratic Assembly
organizations.description: Ba'athist political party in Bahrain (per Wikidata), founded 1991.

organizations.name: National Justice Movement
organizations.description: Political party in Bahrain founded 5 March 2006 (per Wikidata); progressive ideology.

organizations.name: National Liberation Front - Bahrain
organizations.description: Communist party founded 1955; underground for much of its history and the predecessor of the Progressive Democratic Tribune.

organizations.name: Economists Bloc
organizations.description: Political society in Bahrain (per Wikidata); little further structured data available.

organizations.name: Bahrain Defence Force
organizations.description: The military of the Kingdom of Bahrain, under the direct command of a commander-in-chief holding the rank of field marshal; represented in Cabinet by the Minister of Defence Affairs.

organizations.name: Royal Bahraini Army
organizations.description: Ground force component of the Bahrain Defence Force with a current strength of about 20,000 personnel.

organizations.name: Royal Bahraini Air Force
organizations.description: Aerial warfare branch of the Bahrain Defence Force, formed as the BDF Air Wing in 1976 and an independent service branch since 1987.

organizations.name: Royal Bahrain Naval Force
organizations.description: Maritime branch of the Bahrain Defence Force; about 700 personnel and 35 ships, including two former US Oliver Hazard Perry-class frigates.

organizations.name: Bahrain National Guard
organizations.description: Military force separate from the Bahrain Defence Force, charged with internal security; established in 1997 by royal decree of Emir Isa bin Salman Al Khalifa.

organizations.name: National Security Agency
organizations.description: Bahrain's intelligence and secret police agency (also Bahrain Intelligence Agency), created by Decree No. 14 of 2002 to replace the General Directorate for State Security Investigations; associated with but not formally part of the Ministry of Interior.

organizations.name: Public Security Forces
organizations.description: Bahrain's police and law enforcement agency, established 1971, operating under the Ministry of Interior.

top_orgs: Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy (BIRD)
